title: What Is the Golden Hat? The OU-Texas Red River Trophy Explained
question: What is the Golden Hat trophy in the Oklahoma vs Texas game?
answer: The Golden Hat is the trophy awarded on the field to the winner of the Oklahoma-Texas game: a replica of a ten-gallon cowboy hat tied to the State Fair of Texas. It began as a bronze hat, commonly dated to 1941, and turned gold after a 1970s makeover.
summary: The Golden Hat is the Red River Rivalry's on-field trophy, a ten-gallon hat tied to the State Fair of Texas. Learn why it started as the Bronze Hat.
body: Every October in Dallas, the Oklahoma-Texas winner gets more than bragging rights. It carries home the Golden Hat, a replica of a ten-gallon cowboy hat that is about as Texas-State-Fair as a trophy can be. The winning school's athletic department keeps it until the next meeting, when it goes back on the line.

The hat is closely tied to the fair itself. The two schools agreed to play their game in Dallas during the State Fair of Texas starting in 1929, and the fair is credited with donating the trophy. Most rivalry histories date the hat's debut to 1941, though at least one Texas alumni publication ties the fair's gift to 1929, so you will see both years cited.

Here is the trivia twist: it was not always golden. The original was bronze, which is why old-timers called it the Bronze Hat or Brass Hat. The trophy was reworked in the 1970s and came back with a gold finish, giving us the name fans know today.

The hat stays tied to the annual State Fair game, not to any other meeting. When OU and Texas met a second time in the 2018 Big 12 Championship Game, the hat was not at stake, so it stayed in Austin after the Longhorns' regular-season win even though the Sooners won the title game.

For Sooner fans, the image of players hoisting that hat at the Cotton Bowl is one of the best postgame pictures in the sport. It is a small trophy with a big job: settling, for one year, who owns the Red River.
